transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Um… I guess I’m here because flying has gotten really scary for me. Even thinking about getting on a plane brings back this turbulence from my honeymoon flight, and I know people fly safely all the time, but… it’s been hard to shake.
Is it just flying that scares you, or have you noticed yourself feeling anxious in other situations as well?
Mostly just flying. It’s like… the idea of getting on a plane makes me think of that turbulence on my honeymoon flight, and I get scared, even though I know flying is supposed to be safe.
Has your fear of flying stopped you from doing things you want or need to do?

A little, yeah. I’m still doing okay with work and home stuff, but I’ve been skipping some trainings and conferences my supervisor thought would be good for me. And… personal things too, like this Florence trip I was really excited about. I keep putting it off.
Is it the memory of the turbulence on your honeymoon flight that scares you, or is it more the thought of flying in general?
It’s… kind of both. The turbulence is what I picture right away, but now even just thinking about getting on a plane makes me scared, even though I know people fly safely all the time.
Is it only when you think about that specific honeymoon flight that you feel scared, or would the thought of flying in general, without recalling that flight, also scare you?

I think flying in general would still scare me. The honeymoon flight is what pops into my head, but even without focusing on that, just the idea of getting on a plane feels… way scarier than it should.
Do you think you would feel less scared of flying if you couldn't remember the details of that honeymoon flight?

Maybe a little, but… I don’t think it would go away. Even just the idea of getting on a plane feels way scarier than it should. I know people fly safely every day, but my mind still kind of goes there.
Would your fear of flying decrease if you were accompanied by someone you trust on the flight?

Yeah… probably a little. If my husband is with me, I can usually get through talking about a trip without backing out right away. But I’ve still been choosing long drives or skipping work trainings instead of flying, so it doesn’t exactly make it easy.
Would your fear of flying still be present if you were unable to recall the specifics of your honeymoon flight
Yeah… I think it would still be there. Maybe not as sharp, but just thinking about getting on a plane already makes me scared, even if I try not to focus on that flight.
Is there anything specific about the honeymoon flight that you think is causing your fear, or is it just the fact that it was a scary experience?

I think it’s mostly that it was really scary. Like… when I think about flying now, my mind goes right back to that turbulence on our honeymoon flight, even though I know planes are usually safe. Just getting on one feels bigger than it should.
Has your fear of flying affected your relationships with family or friends?

A little, yeah. I mean, I’m still managing things at home and work, but it’s made plans harder. I’ve put off that Florence trip I was excited about, and I’ve passed on some trainings and conferences my supervisor wanted me to go to. So… it hasn’t ruined anything, but it does get in the way.
Do you think your fear of flying would disappear if you never had to fly again

Maybe… if I truly never had to fly, I guess it wouldn’t come up as much. But right now I kind of arrange things around not flying—like driving longer distances or turning down trainings. And if I even have to talk seriously about a trip, I usually need my husband there or I start wanting to back out.
Do you think you would still be afraid of flying if you had never experienced the turbulence on your honeymoon flight?
I don’t know… maybe not this much. I think that turbulence is what my mind goes back to. Flying just feels scarier than it should now, even though I know people do it safely all the time.
Have you experienced anxiety or fear in situations other than flying since your honeymoon flight?
Not really… I mean, I get stressed like anyone, but I haven’t noticed that same kind of fear outside of flying.
Would your fear of flying be less intense if you were to fly a different type of plane or airline than the one you were on during your honeymoon?
I’m not sure it would matter much. I think it’s more the idea of being on a plane at all… I just picture that turbulence again, even though I know flying is usually safe.
Do you think your fear of flying would still be present if you couldn't recall any details of your honeymoon flight at all?
I guess… probably not as much. The fear feels tied to remembering that turbulence. Like, just thinking about getting on a plane brings that back, even though I know flying is safe for most people.
Has your fear of flying been present for more than 6 months?
Yes… it’s been more than six months. It started after that flight back from my honeymoon, so… about two years and five months now.
Has there been any significant life event or change, other than the honeymoon flight, that occurred around the same time your fear of flying started?
Not that I can think of. Nothing major really changed around then… it was mostly just that flight.
Has the fear of flying significantly impacted your daily life or caused you significant distress?

Yeah… I mean, I’m still handling work and things at home. But it has affected stuff. I’ve turned down some trainings and conferences my supervisor thought would be good for me, and I keep putting off personal plans too… like a trip to Florence I was really looking forward to.
Has your fear of flying been persistent and unchanged since it started after your honeymoon flight, or have you noticed any fluctuations in its intensity over time?
It’s been there since that flight coming back from the honeymoon… about two years and five months ago. I don’t know if I’d say it’s changed much.
